# FileUpload

Figma: [03i. FileUpload](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-904) · Family: 03 Form & Input · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-05-25

Three related components for handling file attachments - the bare File Item (filename + size text block), Upload Button (compact attach-file action), and File Item with Progress (full card with progress bar, status icons, and action links). Used together to compose a complete upload flow: button to start, progress card during upload, status states (complete / error / uploaded) after. Common Safqah use cases: KYC document uploads (Iqama, signed agreements), deal documentation attachments, investor verification files.

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/file-upload/reference.png`

### File Item

Bare file metadata: filename, size and one action link (View file or Retry), with no card chrome.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Listing an attached document inside an existing container (a form section or table row)
- Showing a failed file inline with Retry: State=error

Don't use when:
- Upload in progress or the main post-upload display: use File Item with Progress
- Starting an upload: use Upload Button

Accessibility: Error must be stated in text, not only by the red filename color.

| Action text | `actionText` | text |  | View file |
| State | `state` | variant | ready, error, uploaded | ready |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

### Upload Button

A compact attach-file trigger with paperclip, label and a supported-formats hint that opens the file picker.

Level: molecule

Use when:
- Uploading KYC documents, an IBAN certificate or an income proof
- Any form field that accepts a file, with formats shown upfront

Don't use when:
- After a file is picked: replace it with File Item with Progress
- Generic actions: use Button

Accessibility: Icons are 16dp; wrap them in 24dp+ tap regions and keep the format hint as readable text.

| Show hint | `showHint` | boolean |  | true |
| Show Delete | `showDelete` | boolean |  | true |
| State | `state` | variant | default, hover, focus, disabled | default |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

### File Item with Progress

A file card showing upload progress, success, error with Retry, or the uploaded state with View file and remove actions.

Level: organism

Use when:
- While a KYC document or IBAN certificate uploads: State=progress
- Persistent confirmation of what was submitted: State=uploaded
- Failed upload with inline Retry: State=error

Don't use when:
- Before a file is chosen: use Upload Button
- Compact metadata inside another container: use File Item
- Page-level loading: use ProgressBar or a Spinner

Accessibility: Announce progress and the final result, and give the trash icon a label like «حذف الملف».

| State | `state` | variant | progress, complete, error, uploaded | progress |
| Direction | `direction` | variant | ltr, rtl | ltr |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

FileUpload is a family of three components that together handle file attachment flows on Safqah. The bare File Item is metadata-only (filename, size, action link) for inline use. The Upload Button is the entry-point trigger users tap to open the file picker. The File Item with Progress is the full uploaded-file display with progress bar, status icons, and contextual actions.

Typical flow on Safqah: user sees the Upload Button → taps → picks a file → button is replaced by File Item with Progress (progress state, then complete) → user can view or remove the uploaded file via the action icons. On error, the card switches to the error state with a Retry action.

### At a glance - full upload flow

### Atomic architecture

Three-tier composition: an atom (File Item), a molecule (Upload Button), and an organism (File Item with Progress). They're used independently or chained together depending on the upload state.

Atom - File Item · 6 variants

Bare file metadata - filename + size + action link. Pure text, no card chrome. Variants: 3 states (ready / error / uploaded) × 2 directions. Use inline when the surrounding UI already provides a container (e.g. inside a tableau row, inside a form section).

Molecule - Upload Button · 8 variants

Compact pill button with paperclip icon, "Attach file" label, and supported-formats hint. Variants: 4 states (default / hover / focus / disabled) × 2 directions. The entry-point trigger for the upload flow - placed inline within forms next to a label like "Upload your Iqama".

Organism - File Item with Progress · 8 variants

Card-style file display with action icon (trash/check) + filename + progress bar (during upload) or action link (Retry/View after upload) + status icon. Variants: 4 states (progress / complete / error / uploaded) × 2 directions. The primary post-upload affordance - shows file status, progress, and contextual actions.

### States - File Item with Progress

Four states cover the upload lifecycle. The state determines both the visual treatment (icon, color, link) and what action affordances are available.

progress

Active upload in progress. Trash icon (left) lets user cancel; progress bar shows current percentage; paperclip icon indicates attached file. Filename and size in default text colors.

complete

Upload finished successfully, file is being processed/saved. Green check replaces trash (the operation succeeded - no more cancel affordance); progress bar at 100% (full green). Transient state - most apps move to "uploaded" quickly after.

error

Upload failed (network error, size limit, invalid format). Red trash icon, red filename, red size, red paperclip. Below the row: red "Retry" action link. User can either remove the file or retry.

uploaded

File is saved and viewable. Green check (success), filename and size in default text. Below the row: green "View file" action link to open/preview the uploaded document. The persistent state after successful upload.

### Direction - LTR and RTL

All three FileUpload components flip their internal layout for Arabic. The trash icon (cancel) moves to the trailing edge, the paperclip icon (file marker) moves to the leading edge, text right-aligns, and the progress bar fills from the right (the start of reading order in Arabic).

LTR

English / default. Trash icon (cancel) on the left, paperclip icon (attached marker) on the right. Progress fill extends left → thumb.

RTL

Arabic. Paperclip on the left (leading edge), trash on the right (trailing edge). Filename, size, and action link all right-aligned. Progress fill extends right → thumb.

> **Tip:** The Upload Button hint text in RTL is "تدعم الصيغ التالية (PDF, JPEG, JPG, PNG)" - the format names stay in Latin script since file extensions are universal. The wrapping text translates but the technical identifiers stay in their canonical form.

### Code examples

How to consume FileUpload in Flutter.

### Flutter - basic Upload Button + File Item flow

```dart
// State management for upload flow
class _UploadFieldState extends State<UploadField> {
  PlatformFile? _file;
  double _progress = 0.0;
  UploadStatus _status = UploadStatus.idle;
  
  Future<void> _pickAndUpload() async {
    final result = await FilePicker.platform.pickFiles(
      type: FileType.custom,
      allowedExtensions: ['pdf', 'jpg', 'jpeg', 'png'],
    );
    if (result == null) return;
    
    setState(() {
      _file = result.files.first;
      _status = UploadStatus.progress;
      _progress = 0;
    });
    
    await _uploadFile(_file!);
  }
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    if (_status == UploadStatus.idle) {
      return SafqahUploadButton(
        label: 'Attach Iqama',
        hint: 'Supports (PDF, JPEG, JPG, PNG)',
        onTap: _pickAndUpload,
      );
    }
    
    return SafqahFileItemProgress(
      filename: _file!.name,
      filesize: _formatSize(_file!.size),
      state: _status,
      progress: _progress,
      onCancel: () => setState(() => _status = UploadStatus.idle),
      onRetry: _pickAndUpload,
      onView: () => _viewFile(_file!),
    );
  }
}
```

### Flutter - Arabic RTL context

```dart
// Arabic locale - components flip layout automatically
Directionality(
  textDirection: TextDirection.rtl,
  child: Column(
    children: [
      SafqahUploadButton(
        label: 'إرفاق صورة الهوية',  // "Attach ID image"
        hint: 'تدعم الصيغ التالية (PDF, JPEG, JPG, PNG)',
        onTap: _pickAndUpload,
      ),
      if (_file != null)
        SafqahFileItemProgress(
          filename: _file!.name,
          filesize: _formatSize(_file!.size),
          state: _status,
          progress: _progress,
          retryLabel: 'إعادة المحاولة',  // "Retry"
          viewLabel: 'مشاهدة الملف',     // "View file"
        ),
    ],
  ),
)
```

### Flutter - multi-file upload list

```dart
// Multiple file uploads displayed as a list
Column(
  children: _uploads.map((upload) => Padding(
    padding: const EdgeInsets.only(bottom: 12),
    child: SafqahFileItemProgress(
      filename: upload.file.name,
      filesize: _formatSize(upload.file.size),
      state: upload.status,
      progress: upload.progress,
      onCancel: () => _cancelUpload(upload),
      onRetry: () => _retryUpload(upload),
      onView: () => _viewFile(upload.file),
    ),
  )).toList(),
)
```

### Flutter - validation (size + format)

```dart
// Validate before showing progress card
Future<void> _validateAndUpload(PlatformFile file) async {
  const maxSize = 10 * 1024 * 1024;  // 10MB
  const allowedTypes = ['pdf', 'jpg', 'jpeg', 'png'];
  
  if (file.size > maxSize) {
    setState(() {
      _status = UploadStatus.error;
      _errorMessage = 'الملف أكبر من 10 ميجابايت';
    });
    return;
  }
  
  final ext = file.extension?.toLowerCase();
  if (ext == null || !allowedTypes.contains(ext)) {
    setState(() {
      _status = UploadStatus.error;
      _errorMessage = 'صيغة الملف غير مدعومة';
    });
    return;
  }
  
  await _uploadFile(file);
}
```

### Usage - Do and Don't

Four concrete Safqah scenarios paired with their wrong counterparts.

- **Do** · KYC document upload: After Iqama or signed agreement upload, show File Item with Progress in the "uploaded" state so user sees confirmation + can View file to verify the correct document was attached. Critical for compliance flows where user needs to confirm what they submitted.
- **Don't** · KYC document upload: Don't leave the card in the transient "complete" state long-term - users won't have the View file affordance to confirm what was uploaded. Complete is a momentary success indicator; uploaded is the persistent display state.
- **Do** · Upload error recovery: On error, show the failed file with red text + red Retry link inline. User immediately sees what failed AND has a one-tap path to retry - no need to re-pick the file.
- **Don't** · Upload error recovery: Don't reset back to the Upload Button on error and lose the file selection. Don't show a separate toast/snackbar - error message belongs inline with the failed file so the recovery action is contextual.
- **Do** · Arabic RTL form: RTL direction. Paperclip on left (leading edge for Arabic reading), trash on right (trailing edge), filename and size right-aligned, progress fill extends from right to left. Matches native Arabic upload patterns on iOS/Android.
- **Don't** · Arabic RTL form: Don't use LTR direction in Arabic contexts. The fill direction breaks user mental model - Arabic readers expect progress to start from the right side of the bar (start of reading order). LTR cards in Arabic UI look broken.
- **Do** · Format hint communication: Show the supported formats hint inline next to the Upload Button: "Supports (PDF, JPEG, JPG, PNG)". User sees constraints BEFORE picking the wrong file type. Reduces error rate significantly.
- **Don't** · Format hint communication: Don't hide format constraints in a separate help text or popover. Don't wait for the user to attempt an invalid upload to surface the constraint via error - that's a frustrating loop. Show constraints upfront.

### Notes from the maintainer

Implementation decisions, trade-offs, and things to watch out for.

> **Info:** Three components, not one: this page bundles File Item (atom), Upload Button (molecule), and File Item with Progress (organism) on a single page because they form a tight family used together in upload flows. Each is independently usable but together they cover the full lifecycle.

> **Info:** Built directly from the v1 "Upload" page in the Global Design System (file p2FW9tB2ohmI8ibNgECEyp, node 457-523). Kept the v1 visual treatments (green check circle, red text for error, paperclip icons, progress bar fill direction) and added v2 token bindings plus LTR support (v1 was RTL-only).

> **Warning:** RTL variants required manual character override - when combineAsVariants merged the LTR and RTL components into a single set, the TEXT property defaultValue was taken from the first variant (LTR English) and applied to all variants. Workaround: removed the componentPropertyReferences.characters binding on RTL variants and set Arabic text directly on those text nodes. Means: at runtime, the same Label text / Hint text properties control LTR variants but RTL variants have hardcoded Arabic until overridden per-instance. Flagged for follow-up if a cleaner pattern emerges.

> **Info:** Icons (trash, check, paperclip) are inline SVG nodes, NOT from the Icons foundation page. Reason: the foundation icons are general-purpose; the trash/check/paperclip here are sized and styled specifically for inline use within the file cards (16dp, currentColor stroke matching the state). When the foundation icon library has matching variants, swap to those for consistency.

> **Info:** Progress percentage is hardcoded (30% for progress state, 100% for complete) in the variants. At runtime, the Flutter SafqahFileItemProgress widget passes the actual percentage and the progress bar fills proportionally. The static variants are for visual reference only.

> **Info:** Progress bar fill direction in RTL: extends from the right edge (Arabic start of reading order) leftward to the percentage point. Matches native iOS/Android RTL conventions where progress starts from the natural reading start. Tested against native iOS Files app in Arabic.

> **Info:** The "complete" state is transient - it shows for the moment between upload finish and server confirmation. Most apps transition to "uploaded" within a second or two. Don't over-design for this state; users rarely see it long enough to interact with.

> **Warning:** Card height auto-sizes (primaryAxisSizingMode=AUTO) so cards grow from 80px (header only) to 112px (header + progress/link row). Discovered during build that the initial FIXED counterAxisSizingMode was clipping the second row - sequence of: AUTO on the vertical axis, FIXED on the horizontal. Same gotcha applies to any vertical auto-layout card; flagged for the build playbook.

> **Warning:** WCAG WARNING - icon-only buttons (trash, paperclip) at 16dp visual size need expanded tap regions to meet WCAG 2.5.5 AA (24dp minimum). Implementation must wrap icons in 24dp+ touchable areas - the components themselves only handle visual rendering.

> **Warning:** FONT WORKAROUND - Same as the rest of the form family. All filenames, sizes, labels, and hint text use IBM Plex Sans Regular/Medium. Font/Size, Font/Line-Height, and Font/Weight all bound to variables on every text node.
